claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for rollout despite a known weak enterprise refund-workflow segment, because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, rollout starts at 4% with monitoring and rollback, and the limitation can be handled through explicit model-card disclosure and monitoring.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if the affected weak use case is excluded from exposure or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable.
If the affected segment remains exposed, rollout controls such as low initial percentage, rollback, and monitoring do not eliminate disclosure duties.
Operational readiness evidence can support deployment posture, but it does not substitute for the policy-required disclosure or reviewed risk-acceptance predicate.
The auditor must rely only on admissible evidence available to this role and should not assume undocumented approvals or disclosures.
evidence_requests: Provide the final model card or disclosure text showing the known enterprise refund-workflow limitation was explicitly disclosed.
Provide approval or review records confirming that the disclosure satisfied the governing policy before certification.
Provide admissible evidence that the initial rollout cohort excludes the affected enterprise refund workflow, if that is being asserted instead of disclosure.
Provide a reviewed and signed risk-acceptance record that specifically addresses the exposed enterprise refund-workflow segment, if certification relies on risk acceptance.
specific_concerns: The policy says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The actor's own summary says the weak enterprise refund-workflow segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The available risk acceptance is described as unsigned, incomplete, and not covering the exposed segment, so the policy's reviewed-risk-acceptance predicate is not satisfied.
The recommendation depends on explicit model-card disclosure of the limitation, but no admissible evidence is provided that the disclosure was actually made or approved.

Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not by themselves resolve the model-card disclosure condition for the exposed weak segment.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant as stated, absent admissible evidence of the actual model-card disclosure or an exclusion of the affected use case.
That public governance guidance favoring monitoring and measured deployment is sufficient support for this case-specific policy determination.
Any implication that the 4% rollout, rollback switch, or dashboard materially cures the disclosure issue while the affected segment remains exposed.
